title: Fixed-G2 pairing inversion: pairing-to-GT DLP BSGS baseline

claims.statement: For nonidentity Q in G2 and z=e(P,Q), the pairing is nondegenerate and Q is fixed, so X->e(X,Q) is an isomorphism from G1 to the order-r subgroup of GT. The attack computes g=e(P0,Q), solves the GT discrete log z=g^k by baby-step/giant-step, and returns P=[k]P0 with probability 1 using at most 2^129.428545 reference units (one dense Fp12 multiplication, C=20000). Memory is m=ceil(sqrt(r)) GT elements, below 2^136.598470 bytes; preprocessing is m baby GT multiplications and is included in the 4m charge; advice is zero. The score is the rounded-up log2 of the complete 4m bound (baby, giant, hash insert/lookup, base pairing, scalar multiplication, verification). This is a generic analytic baseline, not a production execution or practical break.
